Japanese Particles に, で, を, は and が in Context

Kanjidon Team · Jan 31, 2026

Japanese particles do not map one-to-one onto English prepositions or labels such as “topic” and “subject.” They show how a speaker frames participants, places, paths and events. The same sentence can sometimes take a different particle and remain grammatical while changing focus or construal, so examples need context rather than red crosses.

は and が: Topic, Subject and Focus

は presents a phrase as the topic or contrastive frame. が marks a nominative phrase and often identifies or focuses it. A subject can also be the topic, so “は is never the subject” is false. Context decides what the listener is expected to track.

ContextExampleWhat the particle contributes
Talking about Tanaka田中さんは来ました。Tanaka is the topic; the sentence says he came
Answering 誰が来ましたか田中さんが来ました。Tanaka identifies who came
Introducing yourself normally私は田中です。I is the topic of the introduction
Answering 誰が田中さんですか私が田中です。I identifies the person who is Tanaka

With predicates such as 分かる and 好きだ, the item understood or liked commonly takes が: 日本語が分かります and 猫が好きです. Treat these as construction patterns, not translations of an English verb plus object.

を: Object and Route

  • パンを食べます。—bread is the object of eating.
  • 本を読みます。—the book is the object of reading.
  • 公園を歩きます。—the park is the route or space traversed.
  • バスを降ります。—the bus is the point left with this movement verb.

Potential constructions show why blanket corrections are risky. 日本語が話せる is common, and 日本語を話せる also occurs in contemporary usage. Learn the pattern used by your source and notice the discourse context instead of declaring every を form ungrammatical.

に: Goal, Point, Recipient, Location and Result

  • 学校に行きます。—goal of movement.
  • 七時に起きます。—time point.
  • 先生に質問します。—recipient or target of the question.
  • 机の上に本があります。—location where the book exists.
  • 医者になります。—resulting role or state.

Time expressions do not all require に. Relative expressions such as 今日, 明日 and 毎日 commonly appear without it. Learn time phrases as patterns instead of adding に mechanically.

で: Event Setting, Means, Material and Cause

  • 図書館で勉強します。—setting of the study event.
  • 電車で行きます。—means of transport.
  • 木で机を作ります。—material used.
  • 雨で試合が中止になりました。—cause or circumstance.

A Better Model for に vs で

The familiar state-versus-action mnemonic sometimes predicts beginner examples, but it fails as a rule. 東京に住んでいます uses に because Tokyo is the location selected by 住む. 東京で事故がありました uses で even with ある because Tokyo is the setting of an event. Learn which relationship the predicate creates.

MeaningExampleRoles
Go to school by busバスで学校に行きます。で marks means; に marks goal
Study at school学校で勉強します。で marks the event setting
Go to the library to study図書館に勉強しに行きます。に marks destination; しに marks purpose
A book exists in the library図書館に本があります。に marks location selected by ある

A Better Practice Method

  • Keep the full sentence and the situation that made it natural.
  • Compare two valid sentences and explain the change in focus or relation.
  • Collect examples by predicate, such as 行く, 住む, ある and 勉強する.
  • Check uncertain patterns in a reliable corpus or grammar resource.
  • Avoid correcting a fragment without asking what the speaker meant.
